result.rationale: The handler filters with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, a strict case-sensitive equality, while blacklisted emails are lowercased (`email.toLowerCase()`), implying emails are expected to be compared case-insensitively. A guest 'User@Example.com' already stored as 'user@example.com' passes the filter and is created again via `createMany`, producing a duplicate attendee. The zod schema and frontend Set-based uniqueness check are also case-sensitive, so nothing upstream prevents this.

record.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — Case-sensitive existing-attendee comparison inserts a duplicate when the same email is submitted with different casing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 76 in addGuests.handler.ts, the code filters unique guests with: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. This is a case-sensitive string comparison. If an existing attendee has email 'User@Example.com' and someone tries to add 'user@example.com', the comparison would return false (they're not equal case-sensitively), allowing a duplicate email to be inserted. Email addresses should be compared case-insensitively since email local parts are typically case-insensitive in practice. This is a real bug that could lead to duplicate attendees.
